newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia eyes $5 bln in infrastructure projects.
newsitem.headline: Colombia eyes $5 bln in infrastructure projects.

text.p: About $5 billion will be earmarked for spending on new infrastructure projects in Colombia this year and next, according to senior members of President Ernesto Samper's economic team.

The officials called for the spending for the construction of highways, railways, airports and natural gas distribution networks across the country, after a meeting late Wednesday of the National Council on Economic and Social Policy (Conpes).
Members of the policy-making council include Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo and Cecilia Lopez, head of the National Planning Department.
As outlined in a Conpes document released after Wednesday's meeting, the private sector will be key to the successful completion of the infrastructure projects.
A total of 23 separate bidding processes will be opened between August and October to select the firms that will carry out the projects, either independently or in partnership with the government.
Through the bidding processes, the government's aim would be to raise nearly $2 billion in direct foreign investment, the document said.

The Planning Department's Lopez told a forum on privatization issues last month that Colombia would increase infrastructure investment to 5.55 percent of gross domestic product between this year and 1999 compared to 3.9 percxent over the last two years.
She also said private sector participation in infrastructure investment would almost double to a sum equivalent to 2.56 percent of GDP between 1997 and the end of 1998.
